- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below historical mean.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > +15% above recent high), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +10% above recent peak.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model frequently underreacts; increase forecast by 3–5% to align with sentiment momentum.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; add 2–4% upward bias if sentiment swings >0.5 in 5-day window.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often overpredicts; apply 3–7% downward adjustment if recent 7-day avg sentiment < 0.1.
- Forecast errors cluster near 30-day horizon end; reduce final 5–7 days by 2–5% to account for lagged sentiment effects.
